summary.text: Monica De La Cruz is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Texas's 15th District, which was redrawn in 2025. A Brownsville native and former insurance agency owner, she lost the 2020 race, won the seat in 2022 and was re-elected in 2024. She serves on the House Agriculture and Financial Services committees, and her campaign website says she has secured passage of five pieces of legislation, including a fentanyl-trafficking bill.

paragraphs.text: De La Cruz was born in Brownsville, Texas, in 1974, and graduated from James Pace Early College High School there.
She earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Texas at San Antonio in 1997.
Before running for office she owned and operated an insurance agency and worked as an insurance agent.
She won the July 14, 2020 Republican runoff over Ryan Krause for the 15th District nomination, then lost the November 2020 general election to Democratic incumbent Vicente Gonzalez Jr.
She was first elected to the House in 2022, defeating Democrat Michelle Vallejo, and won re-election against Vallejo in 2024 after winning that year's Republican primary over Vangela Churchill.
She serves on the House Agriculture and Financial Services committees.
In March 2024 she delivered the Republican response to President Biden's State of the Union address in Spanish.

Her House website describes her as the first Republican Latina to represent Texas in Congress and says she has passed three major pieces of legislation into law and resolved nearly 1,500 constituent cases; her campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia, cites five pieces of legislation, including the first bill in nearly 20 years from her community to be signed into law, targeting fentanyl trafficking.

Texas adopted a new congressional map in 2025; a University of Texas at San Antonio professor quoted by Ballotpedia said about 80% of the redrawn 15th District is territory she has not represented in the last two election cycles.
